segments.text: And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
And when Jacob saw them, he said,

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: This is God’s host:
and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.

footnotes: Mahanaim: that is, Two hosts, or, camps

segments.text: And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother unto the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
And he commanded them, saying,

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: Thus shall ye speak unto my lord Esau; Thy servant Jacob saith thus, I have sojourned with Laban, and stayed there until now:

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: And I have oxen, and asses, flocks, and menservants, and womenservants: and I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find grace in thy sight.
¶ And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying,

segments.speaker: Messengers
segments.text: We came to thy brother Esau, and also he cometh to meet thee, and four hundred men with him.
Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed: and he divided the people that was with him, and the flocks, and herds, and the camels, into two bands;
And said,

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: If Esau come to the one company, and smite it, then the other company which is left shall escape.
¶ And Jacob said,

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, the LORD which saidst unto me, Return unto thy country, and to thy kindred, and I will deal well with thee:

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies, and of all the truth, which thou hast shewed unto thy servant; for with my staff I passed over this Jordan; and now I am become two bands.

footnotes: I am not…: Heb. I am less than all

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he will come and smite me, and the mother with the children.

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: And thou saidst, I will surely do thee good, and make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.
¶ And he lodged there that same night; and took of that which came to his hand a present for Esau his brother;
Two hundred she goats, and twenty he goats, two hundred ewes, and twenty rams,
Thirty milch camels with their colts, forty kine, and ten bulls, twenty she asses, and ten foals.
And he delivered them into the hand of his servants, every drove by themselves; and said unto his servants,

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: Pass over before me, and put a space betwixt drove and drove.
And he commanded the foremost, saying,

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: When Esau my brother meeteth thee, and asketh thee, saying, Whose art thou? and whither goest thou? and whose are these before thee?

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: Then thou shalt say, They be thy servant Jacob’s; it is a present sent unto my lord Esau: and, behold, also he is behind us.
And so commanded he the second, and the third, and all that followed the droves, saying,

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: On this manner shall ye speak unto Esau, when ye find him.

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: And say ye moreover, Behold, thy servant Jacob is behind us.
For he said, I will appease him with the present that goeth before me,

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: and afterward I will see his face; peradventure he will accept of me.
So went the present over before him: and himself lodged that night in the company.
And he rose up that night, and took his two wives, and his two womenservants, and his eleven sons, and passed over the ford Jabbok.
And he took them, and sent them over the brook, and sent over that he had.
¶ And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day.

footnotes: breaking…: Heb. ascending of the morning
heading: Jacob Wrestles with God

segments.text: And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him.
And he said,

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: Let me go,
for the day breaketh. And he said,

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.

segments.speaker: The man
segments.text: And he said unto him,
What is thy name?

segments.speaker: The man
segments.text: And he said,
Jacob.
And he said,

segments.speaker: The man
segments.text: Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.

footnotes: Israel: that is, A prince of God

segments.text: And Jacob asked him, and said,

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: Tell me, I pray thee, thy name.
And he said,

segments.speaker: The man
segments.text: Wherefore is it that thou dost ask after my name?
And he blessed him there.
And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel:

segments.speaker: Jacob
segments.text: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.

footnotes: Peniel: that is, The face of God

segments.text: And as he passed over Penuel the sun rose upon him, and he halted upon his thigh.
Therefore the children of Israel eat not of the sinew which shrank, which is upon the hollow of the thigh, unto this day: because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh in the sinew that shrank.
